name: Halvern Steel Safeguard Order
rule_maker: not stated; the Trade Ministry opened the investigation and published the recommendation
enacted: not stated; the recommendation was published on 1 January

source_sentences: Importers of record must pay a tariff of 25% of the customs value on imports of flat-rolled and long steel products, for three years.
A review in the third year may extend it.
Imported fabricated steel products and finished goods containing steel (machinery, vehicles, appliances, fabricated structural sections, fasteners) are not covered.
The Customs Service checks classification at ports and penalizes misdeclaration.
The revenue goes to the general budget.

unclear.text: The standard for "sufficient quantity or quality" is not defined.
readings: U1-a: a product qualifies for exclusion if domestic supply is short in either quantity or quality.
U1-b: a product qualifies for exclusion only if domestic supply is short in both quantity and quality.

unclear.text: A review in the third year may extend it.
readings: U2-a: the tariff lapses at the end of three years unless the third-year review extends it; the length of any extension is not stated.
U2-b: the text gives the review power over the tariff's duration but does not say whether the review must take place or whether the tariff stays in force until it does.

unclear.text: Steel users may apply to exclude a product "not produced domestically in sufficient quantity or quality".
readings: U3-a: an excluded product is no longer subject to the 25% tariff for any importer.
U3-b: the exclusion benefits only the steel user that applied, and other importers of the same product remain subject to the tariff.

context: Halvern is a mid-sized trading country with its own currency and a floating exchange rate. [policy.txt line 3]
Three domestic steel firms supply about 60% of the steel used in Halvern; the rest is imported. [policy.txt line 3]

About 4,000 domestic manufacturers use steel as a main input (machinery, vehicle parts, household appliances, cans, construction products); machinery makers export about 35% of their output. [policy.txt line 3]
Halvern's other large export industries are grain and tourism. [policy.txt line 3]
Halvern buys a small share of the world's steel. [policy.txt line 3]
